Radiology Report
Date: 08/21/2026
Patient: Keila Brakus, 89-year-old female

Examination: MRI thoracolumbar spine

Findings:
MRI thoracolumbar spine 08/21/2026: acute osteoporotic T11 compression fracture with bone marrow edema on STIR imaging.

Impression:
There is an acute osteoporotic compression fracture at the T11 vertebral body, demonstrated by bone marrow edema on STIR sequences. No other acute abnormalities are identified in the thoracic or lumbar spine.

Recommendations:
Clinical correlation is advised. Further management should be guided by the referring physician based on clinical presentation.

Spine Intervention Consultation
Date: 09/01/2026
Patient: Keila Brakus, 89-year-old female

History:
Back pain began 07/08/2026 after bending to pick up a grandchild, 8 weeks before this visit. Seen in the outpatient spine clinic; not hospitalized for this fracture.

Clinical Findings:
Back pain localizes to the fractured level; afebrile with no signs of infection or discitis. Pain NRS 7/10 despite 7 weeks of optimal non-surgical management with oxycodone 5 mg as needed, a thoracolumbar brace and activity modification.

Plan:
Referred for DEXA bone density testing and osteoporosis education; enrolled in the osteoporosis treatment program.

Summary:
The patient presents with persistent localized back pain following a vertebral fracture sustained 8 weeks ago. Current management includes analgesics, bracing, and activity modification. Further evaluation and treatment for osteoporosis are underway.
